title: Man. Post. Cap. II §III: Placeus — distinction not false; Calvin quia intra nos; reatus mediate
pass_a_gloss: PLAC. First let it be; by no necessity, or great utility, I was compelled so to distinguish Adam's sin, provided the distinction is not false, nor harmful, nor wholly useless, it is enough for me. Would that in his book nothing less true, less useful occurred! Next it is not true, what he says, that whoever have spoken of the imputation of Adam's sin understood nothing else by that name than his actual transgression: of which thing those words of mine ought to have admonished him, and as I use Calvin's words, because it is within us, which, because they obstructed his cause, he deliberately omitted. But those words of Calvin are held Comm. on Rom. 5 vs. 17; you have the whole place above p. 92. For the difference which he observes there between Christ and Adam perishes, unless Adam's sin, which is imputed to us, is within us, and holds itself as a quality inhering in us. Third, What he adds that about inhering sin and its imputation it is not treated in this disputation, that itself I say in this place, and that I might say it I employed that distinction. For that which is not controversial among us had to be separated from that which is controversial, and every ambiguity and confusion had to be removed from this question. Which neglected, those who oppose me in this cause do not assault me, but their own shadow. Finally what he says is called into question, whether from that first actual sin of Adam some guilt and some worthiness of penalty lies upon the posterity, is either false, or does not look to me: For I constantly teach that from that sin some guilt and some worthiness of penalty, if yet it is to be called worthiness, lies upon the posterity: I only wish it to lie not immediately but by the mediating corruption which it produced.
pass_b_english: Placeus. First grant it: suppose no necessity or great usefulness compelled me to distinguish Adam's sin this way; so long as the distinction is not false, not harmful, and not wholly useless, that is enough for me. Would that nothing less true or less useful appeared in his book! Next, it is not true that everyone who has spoken of imputing Adam's sin meant by that name only his actual transgression. My own words ought to have warned him of that—and Calvin's phrase, "because it is within us," which he deliberately left out because it hindered his case. Those words of Calvin stand in the Commentary on [[Romans 5.17 >> Bible:Romans 5:17]]; you have the whole place above at p. 92. The difference he marks there between Christ and Adam collapses unless Adam's sin, which is imputed to us, is within us and stands as a quality inhering in us. Third, when he adds that inhering sin and its imputation are not treated in this dispute, I say the same here—and I used the distinction so that I could say it. What is not in controversy among us had to be separated from what is, and every ambiguity and confusion cleared from this question. Neglect that, and those who oppose me in this cause do not fight me but their own shadow. Finally, when he says the question raised is whether from Adam's first actual sin some guilt and some liability to penalty rests on the posterity, that is either false or does not touch me: I constantly teach that from that sin some guilt and some liability to penalty—if liability is even the right word—does rest on the posterity. I only insist that it rests not immediately, but through the corruption that sin produced.
source_text: PLAC. Primum esto; nulla necessitate, vel magna utilitate compulsus peccatum Adae sic distinxerim, modo distinctio non sit falsa, nec noxia, nec prorsus inutilis, mihi satis est. Utinam in eius libro nihil minus verum, minus utile occurreret! Deinde verum non est, quod ait, quicunque de peccati Adae imputatione locuti sunt, eos nihil aliud eo nomine intellexisse, quam ipsius actualem transgressionem: cujus rei eum admonere debuerunt verba illa mea, ac ut verbis utar Calvini, quia intra nos est, quae, quia causae suae oberant, consulto omisit. Habentur autem illa Calvini verba Comm. in Rom. 5. vs. 17. integrum locum habes supra p. 92. Perit enim differentia quam illic observat inter Christum et Adamum, nisi peccatum Adae, quod nobis imputatur, intra nos sit, seque habeat ut qualitas nobis inhaerens. Tertio, Quod addit de peccato inhaerente ejusque imputatione in hac disputatione non agi, id ipsum dico hoc loco, ac ut dicerem distinctionem illam adhibui. Separandum enim fuit id quod non est inter nos controversum ab eo quod controversum est, removendaque ab hac quaestione omnis ambiguitas et confusio. Quo neglecto qui mihi in hac causa adversantur non me oppugnant, sed umbram suam. Denique quod dicit in quaestionem vocari, utrum ex primo illo actuali Adae peccato aliquis reatus et aliqua poenae dignitas posteris incumbat, vel falsum est, vel ad me non spectat: Doceo enim constanter ex illo peccato aliquem reatum et aliquam poenae dignitatem, si tamen dignitas appellanda est, posteris incumbere: tantum volo non immediate sed mediante corruptione quam peperit, incumbere.

choices.choice: Distinction useful; Calvin intra nos; reatus via mediating corruption
